 Live Updates Updated Fri, Nov 6 2026 10:57 AM EST Share Share Article via Facebook Share Article via Twitter Share Article via LinkedIn Share Article via Email Nasdaq attempts to recover from worst rout in 19 months as AI stocks see some buying: Live updates
 Sean Conlon Jenni Reid Lee Ying Shan Paulina Likos Traders work on the floor at the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in New York City, US, Nov. 4, 2026. Jeenah Moon | Reuters The Nasdaq Composite rebounded on Friday as some investors bought the dip in chip stocks following a punishing sell-off that sent the index into correction territory.
 The tech-heavy Nasdaq bounced by 1.6%. The S&P 500 rose 1%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average traded around the flatline.
 Worries of a potential slowdown in data center construction following big Democratic wins in the House and Senate and key state governorships hit U.S. markets hard on Thursday.
 The heavy selling Thursday sent the three major stock averages to their worst one-day losses since April 2025. The Nasdaq Composite tumbled 5.5%, closing more than 10% below its most recent high and putting it in what Wall Street regards as a correction. The broad-market S&P 500 lost 4.4%, while the Dow fell more than 1,800 points, or 3.4%.
 All 11 sectors in the S&P 500 closed lower, but shares of companies tied to the AI build-out led the decline. 
 During Friday's session, shares of Micron Technology were up 5% following a 17% decline on Thursday. Nvidia was up 4% after a 9% rout the day before. 
 "The scale of the falls in some of the market's biggest names has been striking. But it also highlights the concentration risk that has built up in U.S. equity markets," Stuart Clark, portfolio manager at Quilter, said by email.
 "With a relatively small number of technology and semiconductor stocks now carrying so much weight, weakness in those names quickly translates into sizeable falls for the Nasdaq and S&P 500."
 The "Magnificent Seven" stocks shed $1 trillion in total market capitalization on Thursday alone. Along with Nvidia, Tesla , Meta Platforms and Alphabet saw gains Friday.
 Top Democrats have called for the curbing of the data center buildout since the party's big election win. Governor-Elect Gina Hinojosa of Texas, a key data center hub in the country, said in a CNN interview Thursday evening, "We will have laws to protect Texans, and we need to stop what we are doing with data centers until we have those protections."
 Investors reacted to the latest nonfarm payrolls report, which came in much better than expected at an increase of 165,000 in October. That was well above the 59,000 that economists polled by Dow Jones had anticipated. The unemployment rate also moved down to 4.1%. Economists had expected it to hold steady at 4.2%.
 All three major averages are poised for losses on the week, even after Wednesday's big rally in the wake of the election. The Nasdaq is off by almost 3% and the S&P 500 by 2%. The 30-stock Dow is the outperformer, lower by less than 1% week to date.
 Looking at the history of Nasdaq corrections shows tech stocks often find their footing over the next three-to-six months, but trading can remain rocky in the near term.
 40 Min Ago Chip stocks recoup some losses
 Shares of key chipmakers recovered a bit from Thursday's tech-led rout .
 On Friday, shares of Advanced Micro Devices popped 9% after seeing a 17.3% drawdown in the previous session. Intel added almost 7% following its 10.3% decline on Thursday.
 Qualcomm and Micron Technology gained more than 5%. The two dropped 9.5% and 17.5%, respectively, in the prior trading day.
 Nvidia and Marvell Technology advanced more than 4%. The former lost 9.3% Thursday, while the latter shed more than 16%. Broadcom also climbed more than 2%. That stock saw a more than 10% drop Thursday.
 — Sean Conlon 
 1 Hour Ago University of Michigan survey shows surprise uptick in sentiment
 People shop at a discount store in Manhattan on Nov. 7, 2025, in New York City. Spencer Platt | Getty Images Consumers grew a bit more optimistic about the economy heading into the midterm election, according to a University of Michigan survey released Friday.
 The Survey of Consumers for November showed a reading of 51.0, up 6.3% from a month ago and better than the Dow Jones consensus for 47.5. The reading was flat compared to a year ago. Current conditions and expectations indexes also posted monthly gains, up 9.2% and 4.3% respectively.
 The survey period covered Oct. 20-Nov. 2, just before the Tuesday vote.
 On inflation, the one-year outlook slipped to a 4.3% rate, down 0.4 percentage point from October. The five-year view edged lower to 3.4%.
 "While sentiment lifted for lower- and middle-wealth consumers, it fell 5% for those with the largest stock portfolios in the wake of a relatively turbulent period in stock markets," survey director Joanne Hsu said. "Moreover, consumers' comments revealed growing anxiety over a possible AI bubble. AI worries, however, were dwarfed by cost of living concerns, which continue to be at the forefront of consumers' minds across the population."
 — Jeff Cox 
 2 Hours Ago S&P 500, Nasdaq open higher
 The S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite reversed course from the prior day's rout.
 The broad market index rose 0.3% on Friday morning, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq gained 1.1%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average, however, dropped 518 points, or 1%.
 — Sean Conlon 
 2 Hours Ago Ron Baron says Democrats shouldn't go after Musk
 Ron Baron, founder of Baron Capital. Anjali Sundaram | CNBC SpaceX -backer Ron Baron told CNBC on Friday that Democrats shouldn't go after Elon Musk amid controversies about the role of Musk-operated satellites in the war between Russia and Ukraine. Congressional hearings about the matter have been floated in Washington.
 "[Musk] hasn't done anything wrong. Why would there be a hearing?" Baron said on " Squawk Box ."
 Baron made the case that Musk is a good builder and that his various commercial endeavors are supportive of the White House's domestic industrial policies.
 "It would be a bad thing if we were in America reliant on Silicon only coming from Taiwan. [Musk] is probably the only person in this country who is able to build things at scale at attractive prices. Only one," Baron said.
 — Tobias Burns 
 3 Hours Ago U.S. adds 165k jobs in October, beating expectations
 Left to right, Everette Kerry of Life Alert speaks with Maximilian Kegley-Oyola and Dylan Flowers about job opportunities during the Mega JobNewsUSA South Florida Job Fair at Amerant Bank Arena in Sunrise, Florida, Sept. 25, 2026. Joe Raedle | Getty Images The U.S. economy added 165,00 jobs in October , much more than expected, and the unemployment rate slipped slightly to 4.1%. 
 Economists surveyed by Dow Jones expected an increase of just 59,000 jobs. The Bureau of Labor Statistics also revised higher its readings for the prior two months, with a combined 84,000 more jobs added than previously reported. 
 — Davis Giangiulio 
 3 Hours Ago Moderna, Lam Research and Five9 among the stocks making moves before the bell
 Check out some of the companies making the biggest moves premarket: 
 Moderna — The vaccine maker rallied nearly 10%. The company smashed third-quarter earnings and estimates and raised its outlook for full-year sales growth. Moderna now expects 2026 revenue growth of 15% to 25%, up from previous guidance of no more than 10%. 
 Lam Research — The semiconductor equipment maker surged nearly 11% after the board authorized a $25 billion stock buyback.
 Five9 — The cloud-based Contact Center as a Service provider fell more than 17% premarket. Five9 lowered full-year adjusted EPS guidance and announced a $325 million cash acquisition of Level AI.
 Read here for the full list of names.
 — Deena Zaidi 
 3 Hours Ago What to expect with the upcoming October jobs report
 A job seeker fills out a request for information during the HIRE360 Diversity Hiring Expo & Mega Career Expo at the Carson Event Center on June 30, 2026, in Carson, California. Justin Sullivan | Getty Images The U.S. economy isn't expected to have produced much job growth in October, with employers reluctant to hire workers but also not cutting staff amid a shrinking labor force and a growing problem of long-term unemployment.
 Economists are looking for a meager nonfarm payrolls gain of 59,000, a slight uptick from the 29,000 jobs produced in September, according to the Dow Jones consensus. That result would continue a pattern of sparse growth.
 But that's kind of OK: The forecast also is that the unemployment rate will hold at a very low 4.2% rate, the product of a climate where a stagnant labor force reduces the need for outsized job increases to keep the jobless level steady.
 "Long-term, we're not going to need as many jobs added to the economy to have stable employment because we have fewer people who are available to work," said Nicole Bachaud, labor economist at jobs site ZipRecruiter. "An aging workforce is pushing a lot of people into retirement. We have had decades of low birth rates, meaning we don't have a lot of people who are coming in to replace those retiring workers. And immigration is now down pretty significantly, which is reducing some of that prime-age employment."
 Read the full story here .
 — Jeff Cox 
 4 Hours Ago Trump reiterates support for AI after Democratic midterm victories
 U.S. President Donald Trump speaks during an event in the Oval Office of the White House on Nov. 5, 2026 in Washington, DC. Andrew Harnik | Getty Images President Donald Trump on Friday said he 100% is in favor of the artificial intelligence build-out, and will work with any state that wants to help support the technology's growth. 
 "They are GOLD, and only foolish leadership will say "NO" to the riches they bring!" he said in a post on Truth Social . 
 The post comes after many Democrats won races in the 2026 midterm elections on Tuesday by campaigning against data centers , the key facilities that are in high demand to help support AI. Some of those Democrats, at both the national and state level, have called for data center moratoriums. 
 — Davis Giangiulio 
 5 Hours Ago European stocks lower, U.S. tech set for rebound
 European stock markets remained deeply in the red on Friday, with the regional Stoxx 600 index last down 1.7%, heading for its worst session since March. Tech continued to be one of the most resilient sectors, down just 0.2%. 
 U.S. tech looked broadly set for a rebound, according to premarket indicators. 
 The five worst performers from the Nasdaq on Thursday were all higher in premarket on Friday, with SanDisk Corporation last seen up 9.6%, Astera Labs up 8.1%, Lumentum Holdings up 8.55%, Micron Technology up 8.2% and Western Digital up 6.6%.
 — Jenni Reid 
 6 Hours Ago Oil prices set for sharp weekly fall after midterm elections as investors weigh Iran conflict risk
 Fuel tankers carrying Iraqi oil arrive at the coastal storage facilities of the Baniyas Oil Terminal in Tartus province, Syria, on September 13, 2026. Hasan Belal | Anadolu | Getty Images Oil prices rebounded a touch on Friday, extending earlier gains, as investors weighed the risk of renewed military escalation between the U.S. and Iran following the midterm elections, alongside prospects for a diplomatic breakthrough.
 International benchmark Brent crude futures were recently higher by 36 cents, or 0.39%, to $98.65 a barrel, having jumped to almost $100 a barrel earlier in the session. U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude futures were ahead 43 cents or 0.48% to $90.98 a barrel.
 Oil prices set for sharp weekly fall after midterm elections as investors weigh Iran conflict risk 8 Hours Ago European stocks plunge at the open as sell-off spreads
 watch now VIDEO 2:08 02:08 AI meltdown sends markets reeling Squawk Box Europe The pan-European Stoxx 600 index was 1.26% lower in early deals, following deep losses in Asia-Pacific markets on Friday and a sell-off on Wall Street on Thursday . 
 All sectors were in the red, though technology saw among the smallest impact, down 0.8%. Media stocks tumbled 2.4% as health-care fell 2.2%.
 — Jenni Reid 
 9 Hours Ago AI sell-off is an adjustment to sustainable growth expectations: portfolio manager
 The sharp sell-off in AI-related names this week reflects an adjustment in growth expectations to a more sustainable level, according to William de Gale, co-founder and lead portfolio manager at Blue Box Asset Management — but it does not change "insatiable" levels of demand.
 De Gale told CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe" that the technology sector had been delivering consistent profits and stock price growth of around 15% for nearly two decades. This was connected to a host of supply constraints, including in semiconductor equipment, raw materials, energy, staffing and permitting, which cap the growth rate, he said. 
 "AI has been able to grow a lot faster than that in recent years because it's been a lot smaller. It's a subset of the tech sector by and large, but eventually it becomes big enough that it runs into that overall constraint, and I think that's really what's happening now," de Gale said.
 "The industry seems to be ahead of what expectations are, ahead of what is sustainable, and at the moment, all the models have 30% top line growth in them, going many years into the future, and nothing that big can grow that fast very long, so those models all need to come down to 15, to 20%, and that's the adjustment that's happening at the moment."
 "I don't think there's any real issue with demand. The demand is insatiable, and the demand outside AI is pretty much insatiable as well."
 watch now VIDEO 6:16 06:16 Software stocks are a great place to hide, says portfolio manager Squawk Box Europe — Jenni Reid 
 9 Hours Ago Asia-Pacific markets close in the red as tech rout deepens
 Asia-Pacific markets tumbled on Friday, as a sharp sell-off in technology stocks swept across the region.
 South Korea's Kospi fell more than 6%, leading losses in the region to end at 5,059.69, and declining 11.7% this week. The small-cap, tech-focused Kosdaq fell 5.03%, closing at 644.27.
 Japan's  Nikkei 225 dropped 5.96% to 57,434.77, entering bear market territory. 
 Mainland China's CSI 300 fell 1.44% lower at 4,054.28, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng was down 1.32% as of its last hour of trade.
 Taiwan's Taiex also entered bear market, dropping 4.51% to 39,701.64. Australia's S&P/ASX 200 was down 0.49% at 9,020.8.
 — Lee Ying Shan 
 10 Hours Ago Daimler Truck profit up 89% as U.S. truck sales rebound from tariff uncertainty
 The Daimler logo hangs on a wall at Daimler Freightliner truck assembly plant, after U.S. President Donald Trump announced on Thursday that he would impose a 25% duty on imports of heavy-duty trucks starting October 1, in Derramadero, Coahuila state, Mexico, September 27, 2025. Antonio Ojeda | Reuters Germany's Daimler Truck reported an 89% year-on-year increase in earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT) to 1.05 billion euros ($1.18 billion).
 North American truck sales jumped 51%, which the company attributed to both a continued market recovery and the impact of tariff uncertainty in the same quarter last year. The North American market for heavy-duty trucks fell 7% in the first three quarters, but was offset by 8% growth in Europe. 
 Daimler, one of the world's biggest truck manufacturers, flagged ongoing market challenges, including slowing growth, rising energy costs and uncertainty in the global economy. 
 CFO Eva Scherer said the company showed "discipline in converting performance into cash" in the quarter and was "determined to maintain that discipline."
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon Daimler Truck. — Jenni Reid 
 11 Hours Ago Oil prices could spike as U.S. action on Iran nears: Rapidan Energy
 The U.S. is likely to resume military action against Iran in the coming days, a move that could send oil prices sharply higher, according to Bob McNally, CEO at geopolitical and energy analysis firm Rapidan Energy Group.
 Speaking to CNBC's " Squawk Box Asia ," McNally put the odds of "a resumption of military fighting" at 80% as the U.S. midterm elections recede.
 McNally said he expects both Brent and West Texas Intermediate crude futures to rise above $100 a barrel. The benchmarks are currently trading at about $100 and $91, respectively.
 "President Donald Trump is determined, as a legacy item, almost at all costs, to prevent Iran from getting a nuclear weapon, having them give up their nuclear capabilities," McNally said.
 "The Iranian regime, on the other hand, is not willing to do it. And as long as that core difference in that deal space is absent, the escalation dynamic remains in place," he added.
 — Lim Hui Jie 
 15 Hours Ago SK Hynix, Samsung, SoftBank, TSMC tumble as Asian chip stocks track U.S. AI sell-off
 Asian technology stocks tumbled Friday, tracking a sharp sell-off on Wall Street overnight that sent the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite into correction territory as renewed concerns over artificial intelligence spending rattled investor sentiment.
 South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix plunged over 8%, while Samsung Electronics shed 7%. LG Innotek and LG Display fell 10% and 7.7%, respectively, as selling pressure spread across the country's technology sector.
 The rout came as investors worried that Democrats' sweeping victory in the U.S. midterm elections could lead to tighter restrictions on data-center build-out, potentially slowing demand for AI chips and related infrastructure. 
 In Japan, semiconductor-related stocks also fell, with chip-testing equipment maker Advantest plunging 12.2%, while Tokyo Electron slid 7.3%. Technology investment giant SoftBank Group tumbled 11.6%.
 Shares of memory chipmaker Kioxia Holdings fell nearly 10%, while Renesas Electronics declined 7.5%.
 In Taiwan, semiconductor stocks also came under heavy selling pressure, with contract chipmaker TSMC sliding 9.6%. Electronics manufacturers Hon Hai Precision Industry , also known as Foxconn, and Foxconn Technology fell 9.4% and 9.1%, respectively, as the regional technology rout deepened.
 — Lee Ying Shan 
 16 Hours Ago Texas Governor-elect Hinojosa says it’s possible to work with Musk ‘on our terms’
 State Representative Gina Hinojosa, a Democrat from Texas and gubernatorial candidate, speaks during a campaign event with State Representative James Talarico, a Democrat from Texas and US Senate candidate, not pictured, at the Stubbs - Waller Creek Amphitheater in Austin, Texas, US, on Monday, Nov. 2, 2026. Jordan Vonderhaar | Bloomberg | Getty Images Texas Governor-Elect Gina Hinojosa said in a CNN interview Thursday that under Democrats' leadership, the state could still have a "strong working relationship" with Elon Musk and his companies, but that deals would have to be done "on our terms." 
 As a candidate, Hinojosa made AI data center regulation a big focus of her campaign. She also said during the interview, "We need to stop what we are doing with data centers until we have measures to protect Texans." 
 Musk's automaker Tesla and aerospace and defense tech conglomerate SpaceX are both headquartered in Texas, and are jointly developing a chips factory and data center at a sprawling industrial complex called Terafab in Grimes County, Texas.
 Hinojosa on Thursday also requested that Texas Parks and Wildlife pause talks of a public land sale to SpaceX, which would help expand the company's Starbase launch facility in the far south of the state.
 — Lora Kolodny 
 16 Hours Ago Japan's Nikkei 225 enters bear market territory; Kospi plunge triggers circuit breakers 
 Japan's Nikkei 225 entered bear market territory Friday, as a deepening sell-off in technology stocks dragged the benchmark more than 20% below its June peak.
 Chip-related stocks led losses, with Advantest plunging 12% and SoftBank Group shedding 11%. Semiconductor equipment maker Tokyo Electron fell nearly 9%, while chipmaker Kioxia Holdings dropped 11%.
 Separately, South Korea's benchmark Kospi fell deeper into bear market, plunging more than 8% in early trading Friday, triggering circuit breakers with trading suspended for 20 minutes.
 — Lee Ying Shan 
 16 Hours Ago South Korea's Kospi plunges 8% as Asia markets tumble after Wall Street AI rout
 Asia-Pacific markets tumbled Friday, tracking a sharp sell-off on Wall Street overnight that saw the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite slide into correction territory amid renewed concerns over artificial intelligence stocks.
 South Korea led losses in the region, with the Kospi plunging more than 8% to slip below the 5,000 mark, while the small-cap Kosdaq shed over 7%.
 Japan's  Nikkei 225 fell than 2%, while the broader Topix index declined 2.9%.
 Australia's S&P/ASX 200 slipped 0.9%.
 — Lee Ying Shan 
 17 Hours Ago Trump says Democrats are to blame for the stock market suffering
 US President Donald Trump speaks in the Oval Office of the White House, Washington, DC, on Nov. 5, 2026. Mandel Ngan | AFP | Getty Images President Donald Trump said, "The Stock Market suffered one of the Worst Days in History based on the results of the Election," in a post on Truth Social, late Thursday.
 The S&P 500, Nasdaq, and Russell 2000 all saw their worst sessions since April 2025, according to FactSet.
 The artificial intelligence-driven sell-off pushed the tech-heavy Nasdaq into correction territory.
 Democrats' big wins in the House and Senate ignited worries of a potential slowdown in data center construction.
 — Paulina Likos 
 17 Hours Ago Asia-Pacific markets set to plunge after AI sell-off sinks Wall Street
 Asia-Pacific markets were set to open sharply lower Friday, tracking steep losses on Wall Street as a sell-off in technology stocks sent the Nasdaq Composite into correction territory.
 Futures for Japan's  Nikkei 225  in Chicago were at 57,110 while in Osaka they were last at 57,400, compared with the index's previous close of 61,077.9.
 Futures for Hong Kong's Hang Seng index last traded at 24,494 compared with the index's last close of 24,796.98.
 Australia's S&P/ASX 200 was down over 1% in early trade.
 Concerns over the implications of a Democratic sweep in the U.S. midterm elections for the artificial intelligence sector have dented sentiment around AI plays, already under scrutiny over capex, profitability and debt. 
 — Lee Ying Shan 
 17 Hours Ago Job growth in October is expected to come in at 59,000, per Dow Jones
 The Bureau of Labor Statistics will release the October nonfarm payrolls Friday.
 Economists are expecting growth of 59,000 jobs, an increase from the 29,000 jobs produced in September, according to the Dow Jones consensus
 The unemployment rate is forecast to hold at 4.2%.
 The Federal Reserve sees the labor market as being on a solid footing, although uncertainty remains. 
 The market is pricing in about a 70% chance of a 25-basis point interest rate hike at its Dec. 9 meeting, according to the CME FedWatch Tool .
 — Paulina Likos 
 17 Hours Ago Megacap tech's 'Magnificent Seven' lost more than $1 trillion in market value
 The "Magnificent Seven" lost more than $1 trillion in aggregate market cap in Thursday's tech-led sell-off.
 Nvidia led the way, losing more than $440 billion in market value. 
 Shares of the AI chip leader fell more than 9% and turned negative on the year. 
 The stock is now down 2.6% for the year.
 Tesla sank 10.8%, Meta fell 3.9%, Microsoft shed 3.6%, Alphabet closed down 2.2%, Amazon fell 2.2% and Apple dropped 1.5%.
 — Paulina Likos 
 17 Hours Ago Stocks making the biggest moves after hours: DraftKings, Airbnb & more
 Several stocks saw dramatic moves in extended trading as another raft of earnings releases rolled out: 
 DraftKings — The online sports betting platform tanked 24% after the company posted a wider-than-expected third-quarter loss. DraftKings posted a loss of 94 cents per share, worse than the 39 cents per share loss analysts polled by LSEG anticipated. Revenue of $1.33 billion fell short of the $1.40 billion estimate. Sportsbook revenue for the period came in at $784 million, missing the $811.8 million StreetAccount consensus estimate.
 Airbnb — The vacation rental platform jumped 11%. Airbnb reported third-quarter earnings of $3.16 per share, topping analysts' consensus estimate of $2.85, while revenue of $4.87 billion beat the Street's $4.75 billion, LSEG data showed.
 Iren – The neocloud reported first fiscal quarter revenue of $228 million, up from $137 million in the prior quarter. Iren also said that more than $4 billion in annual recurring revenue that was projected to arrive in 2026 has been delayed until at least January 2027. Shares gained 4% in extended trading. The stock has been battered in the latest rout of artificial intelligence-focused names, dropping 31% in the past week.
 Read more about Thursday's after-hours movers here .
 — Darla Mercado 
 17 Hours Ago Stock futures fall Thursday evening
 U.S. stock futures fell shortly after 6 p.m. ET on Thursday.
 Futures linked to the S&P 500 were down 0.4%, while Nasdaq-100 futures dropped 0.4%. Dow futures lost 201 points, or 0.4%.
 — Darla Mercado
